caption: Car into turning tractor-semitrailer at an uncontrolled median crossover, US-27A near Williston, Florida (2016)

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: We are on the record. This is the videotaped deposition of Witness B, taken in

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: connection with the wrongful death action arising from the collision on U.S. Highway 27A at

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Northeast 140th Court in Levy County, Florida, on May 7, 2016. Today's date is the

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: fourteenth. The time is 9:42 a.m. Counsel, please state your appearances for the record.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: I represent the estate of the driver of Vehicle

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: A, and I'll be conducting the examination this morning.

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Appearing on behalf of the defendant motor carrier and the driver of

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Vehicle T. We'll reserve all objections except as to form until the

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: time of trial, and the witness will read and sign.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Agreed. The witness has been sworn by the court reporter off camera. Good morning.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Good morning.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: You understand you're under oath, the same oath you would take

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: in a courtroom in front of a judge and a jury?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes, I understand.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Have you ever given a deposition before?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. Never. I've been on jury duty once but that's it.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Then let me go over a few ground rules. They make the record cleaner

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: and they make this go faster. The court reporter is taking down everything we

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: say, and the camera is recording you. So I'll ask that you answer out

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: loud. Nods and shrugs don't come through on the transcript. Okay?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Okay.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Try to let me finish my question before you start your answer, even if you know

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: where I'm going. And I'll try to let you finish your answer before I start the

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: next question. If we talk over each other, the reporter can't get either of us. Fair?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: That's fair.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: If you don't understand a question, tell me and I'll rephrase it. If

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: you answer, I'm going to assume you understood it. Is that all right?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: From time to time the other attorney may object. Unless one of us tells you

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: not to answer, you can go ahead and answer after the objection. If you need

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: a break at any time, just say so. The only thing I ask is that

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: you not take a break while a question is pending. Do you understand?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I understand.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Is there any reason, any medication or illness or anything else,

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: that would keep you from giving full and truthful testimony today?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. I'm a little nervous but that's it.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: That's completely normal. Did you do anything to prepare for today?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I met with the lawyer, with him, for about an hour last week.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: And I read over the statement I gave to the deputy back then.

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Just so the record is clear, she's referring to me, and I'll instruct

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: the witness not to reveal the substance of any conversations with counsel.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Understood. I'm not asking what was said. Other than the statement to the

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: deputy, did you look at any documents, photographs, videos, anything like that?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: They showed me some pictures of the intersection. Just the road. And a map.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Do you remember if it was the same map we'll be using today?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I think so. It looked like a drawing, from the top, with the roads.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Okay. We'll get to that. Let's start with a little background. How old are you?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I'm forty-three.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: And where do you live? I don't need a street address, just the general area.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I live outside Williston, maybe six or seven miles from that intersection. Toward Bronson.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: How long have you lived in that area?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Going on eleven years.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: What do you do for work?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I'm a home health aide. I go to people's houses, mostly older folks,

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: and help them with bathing, medications, getting around. That kind of thing.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Were you working in that job in May of 2016?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes, same agency. I've been there about nine years now.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Do you drive as part of your job?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Every day. I drive all over the county. Back then I had a

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: lot of clients out along 27A, so I was on that road constantly.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: So you're familiar with that stretch of highway.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Very familiar. I could drive it with my eyes closed. Not that I would.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Do you wear glasses or contact lenses?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Contacts. For distance. I'm nearsighted.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Were you wearing your contacts on the afternoon of May 7th, 2016?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes. I put them in every morning. I don't go anywhere without them.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: When was your last eye exam before the accident?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: That January, I think. I get them checked every year because of the driving.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Any problems with your hearing?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: All right. Let's talk about May 7th, 2016. Do

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: you remember what day of the week that was?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: It was a Saturday. I remember because I wasn't

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: working, I had the day off, which is rare.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: What were you doing that afternoon, before the collision?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: My car was in the shop, the transmission, so my sister was driving me around

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: to run errands. She dropped me at the store on the corner there to pick

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: up a few things while she went down the road to drop off something at

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: a friend's house. She was going to come back and get me.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: When you say the store on the corner, which store do you mean?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: The little store right there at the intersection, on the south

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: side of the highway, where 140th Court goes off. It's like

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: a convenience store, feed and supplies, a little bit of everything.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Approximately what time did your sister drop you off?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: A little after four. Maybe ten after four. I know it was after

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: four because she was complaining about missing the start of a ball game.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: How long were you inside the store?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Not long. Fifteen, twenty minutes. I bought some things

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: and then I went outside to wait for her.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: What did you buy, if you remember?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Dog food, a bag of ice, a couple of drinks. I

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: remember the ice because by the end of everything it had

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: all melted in the bag. I just left it sitting there.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: When you went outside, where did you go?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I went out front to wait. There's a little bench out there with a roof over

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: it, kind of like a bus stop. I sat there for a while with my bags.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: What was the weather like?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Hot. Sunny. It was a clear day. No rain at all. I

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: remember I was glad there was a roof over the bench.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Was the road wet or dry, as far as you could tell?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Dry. It hadn't rained in a while, I don't think.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Where was the sun, if you recall?

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Object to form.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: You can answer.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Up high. It was still afternoon. It was over toward the west,

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: you know, but still pretty high. It wasn't in my eyes, if

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: that's what you're asking. I had the roof over me.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did you have sunglasses on?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. They were in my sister's car.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: While you were sitting on the bench, what were you doing?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Just waiting. I had my phone out for a bit, I was

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: texting my sister asking where she was. Then I put it away

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: and I was just watching the road, watching for her car.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Do you remember roughly how long you were outside before the collision happened?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Maybe five, ten minutes. Not long.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Which direction would your sister have been coming from?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: From the west. From the Bronson side. So I was

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: looking that way, up toward the hill, watching for her.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Tell me about the hill.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: If you're on the south side looking west, the highway goes up a rise. It's not

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: a big hill, it's Florida, but it's enough that cars just kind of appear over the

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: top of it. You can't see past it. Then they come down toward the intersection.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: About how far away is the top of that rise from the intersection, if you know?

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Object to form. Calls for speculation.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I don't know exactly. A quarter mile? Less? A

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: few hundred yards. I'm not good with distances.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: That's fine. Tell me about the traffic that afternoon. Was it busy?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. It was pretty quiet. Saturday afternoon out there, there's

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: not a lot going on. A car every so often.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: At some point did you notice a tractor-trailer?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes. There was a big truck on the other side of the

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: highway, the north side. It was in the turn lane, the one

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: in the middle where you turn left to cross over.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Which direction had that truck been traveling?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: It was going west. It was on the westbound side, heading toward Bronson, and

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: it was waiting in the left turn lane to come across to 140th.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Can you describe the truck?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: A regular big rig. The trailer was white, a box trailer. It had

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: one of those refrigeration units on the front of the trailer, I could

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: hear it humming. The cab was darker. I don't remember the exact color.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: When you first noticed the truck, was it moving or stopped?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Honestly, I couldn't tell you for sure. It was either stopped or barely

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: moving. It was just kind of sitting there in the turn lane, creeping.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did you watch the truck make its turn?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes. It started to come across, real slow. It came out of the turn lane,

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: across the median part, and started across the eastbound lanes, toward our side, toward 140th.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: When you say slow, can you give me any idea of the speed?

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Object to form.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Walking speed? A little faster than walking, maybe. It was

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: a big truck making a tight turn. They go slow.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did the truck have its turn signal on?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I don't remember. I didn't notice either way.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Okay. At some point did you notice another vehicle?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes. The car.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Tell me what you saw.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I was looking up toward the hill for my sister and a car came over the

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: top. Eastbound, coming toward the intersection, on the side closest to me. And I remember thinking,

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: at first, is that her? But it wasn't her car. Hers is a minivan.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Was the truck already moving when you first saw the car come over the rise?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Let me think. I think the truck was still in the turn lane when

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: the car came over the hill. It started across after. Not long after.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Can you describe the car?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: A sedan. Lower, sleek. Darker color. I didn't know what

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: kind it was at the time. I found out later.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did the car have its headlights on?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. It was the middle of the afternoon. I don't think anybody had headlights on.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Which lane was the car in?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: The right lane. The outside lane, closest to my side, closest to the store.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did the car change lanes at any point as it came down the hill?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. It stayed right in that lane. Just straight.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Could you tell how fast the car was going?

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Object to form. Foundation.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: You can answer if you're able.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: It was moving along pretty good. I couldn't give you a

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: number. I'm not good with speeds any more than distances.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: What gave you that impression?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Just how quick it came down the hill. One second it

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: was at the top and then it was right there.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Where was the truck by the time the car got near the intersection?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: The truck was across the road by then. Across the lane the car was in.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did you see the car's brake lights come on at any point?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. I couldn't see the back of it anyway, it was coming

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: toward me. But it never slowed down that I could see.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did you hear any braking? Tires squealing, anything like that?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. Nothing. No tires, no horn. There was nothing until the crash.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did you hear the truck's horn?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. I don't remember any horn.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: We've been going about forty minutes on my watch. Let's take a short break. Five minutes.

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: That's fine.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: We're going off the record.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: We're back on the record. You understand you're still under oath?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did you speak with anyone about the substance of your testimony during the break?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. I went to the restroom and got some water.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Before the break we were talking about the car coming down the hill. I want to

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: talk about the collision itself. Tell me what you saw and heard when the collision happened.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: The truck was across the eastbound lanes, the trailer was stretched across the road,

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: and the car went right into the side of it. Right under it. There

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: was this terrible noise, like a bang and a tearing sound at the same

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: time. And then the car just kept going out the other side.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: When you say it kept going, which direction did the car go?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: East. It came out from under the trailer and kept going east, down the highway, and

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: then drifted off the road to the right side. Off my side of the road.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did it slow down at all after it came out from under the trailer?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Not much. It went a long way. It went off the road into the grass

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: and through a fence and I heard it hit something. I found out later it

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: hit a pole. Then it ended up way down there in somebody's yard.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: How far down the road did the car go before it stopped, if you know?

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Object to form.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Far. Down past a couple of houses. I've heard people say it

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: was hundreds of feet. I believe that. It just kept going.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: What did the truck do after the impact?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: It kept going too, slow. It finished the turn and pulled down 140th

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Court and stopped. Past the store, down the side road a little way.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: What did you do?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I stood up. I think I dropped my bag. I just stood there for a second.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Then I started walking toward the road but I didn't know what to do. A man

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: came out of the store and he was on the phone with 911 already.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did you go to the car?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. It was too far down. Some other people ran down there. I

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: stayed by the store. I was shaking. I'm not ashamed to say it.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did you speak with the driver of the truck?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. I didn't talk to anybody from the truck.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did you speak with law enforcement at the scene?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes. A deputy came and took my information and asked me what I saw.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Later on, I wrote out a statement. That's the one I looked at.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: About how long after the crash did you give that statement?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: The written one was a few days later. They called me.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: When your sister came back, where were you?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Still by the store. She couldn't get through because of all the emergency vehicles, so she

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: parked across and walked over. She stayed with me while I talked to the deputy.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Have you discussed what you saw with your sister?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Of course. Many times. She was upset for me.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Has anything your sister said affected your memory of what you saw?

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Object to form.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. She didn't see anything. She was down the road.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Have you read any news articles about the crash?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Some. It was on the local news for a

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: while. I tried not to read too much.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Have you watched any videos or reconstructions about it?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No. I saw something on TV once, a picture

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: of the car, and I turned it off.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: I want to go back to the moments right before impact.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Where was the trailer when the car reached the intersection?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: It was across both eastbound lanes. The cab had already made it to the other

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: side, onto 140th, kind of, and the trailer was stretched across the road behind it.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: From where you were, could you see the road on the far side of the truck?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: The far side. You mean the north side? Parts of it. Under

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: the trailer, a little, and around it. It's a big trailer.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Could you see the car the whole time as it came down the hill?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Most of the way, yes. I had a good view up the hill.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Do you remember what you were looking at, specifically, right before the impact?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: The car. I was watching the car the whole time, because I knew

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: it was going to hit. I couldn't take my eyes off it.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Let's mark an exhibit. I'm handing you what's been

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: marked as Exhibit 4. Do you recognize it?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes. That's the map I saw before. The drawing of the intersection.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: For the record, Exhibit 4 is a schematic top-down diagram of the intersection of U.S. 27A

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: and Northeast 140th Court. North is toward the top of the page. There's a scale bar

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: at the bottom. Do you see the highway running left to right across the page?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: And do you see the side road, 140th Court, going

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: down from the highway toward the bottom of the page?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes, I see it.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: And the building at the lower right of the

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: intersection, is that the store you were at?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: That's the store. Yes.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Using this red pen, could you please put a small mark

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: where the truck came to a stop after the collision?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: It was down here. Down 140th, past the store. About here.

exhibit.note: Witness B marks where Vehicle T stopped on NE 140th Court, south of the store (consistent with NTSB/HAR-17/02 p.1)

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Let the record reflect the witness has made a mark on NE 140th

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Court, south of the store. Thank you. Now, I'd like you to show

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: us where you were standing at the moment of the collision.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I was over by the corner, near the shelter.

exhibit.note: Witness B marks an X just south of the eastbound shoulder and east of NE 140th Court, in front of the store near the bench shelter. Spoken only as 'over by the corner, near the shelter'. Marked position (7.5, 6.5) m; eye height ~1.6 m standing.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Let the record reflect the witness has placed a mark on

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Exhibit 4. Were you sitting or standing at that moment?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Standing. I'd stood up when I saw the truck pulling across. I

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: stood up because I could tell something was going to happen.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: From that spot, in the last second or so before

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: the car hit the trailer, what did you see?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I had a clear view of the car the whole way in. I watched

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: it right up until the moment it hit. Nothing was in the way.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: You're telling us you could see the car itself, the

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: front of it, in that last second before impact.

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Objection. Asked and answered.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: You can answer.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: Yes. I saw it clearly, the whole time, right up

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: until it went under the trailer. I'll never forget it.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Where was the truck's trailer at that moment, relative to you and the car?

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Object to form.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: It was across the road. The car was coming at it.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I could see the car. I'm sure of what I saw.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Did you tell the deputy at the scene that you

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: watched the car all the way in to the impact?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I don't remember if I said it that way that day.

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I was very upset. I know I've said it since.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Is it in your written statement?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: I don't think it's in there, no. I wrote down the

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: main things. The truck turning and the car not stopping.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: All right. Thank you. I'll pass the witness.

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: I have just a couple of questions. Ma'am, the car you saw come

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: over the hill, did it ever slow down before it reached the truck?

states.speaker: Witness B
states.text: No, sir. Not that I could see.

states.speaker: Opposing counsel
states.text: Nothing further.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: Nothing further from me. We'll go off the record.

states.speaker: Attorney
states.text: The time is 10:16 a.m. This concludes the deposition.
